ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

2. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

3. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

6. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

7. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

9. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

10. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

11. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Word Class: Adverbs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listenin and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

8. B — Where is the library?

16. (4 marks)
